## Deck Goal
Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers to keep HTL readable, markup-focused and context-safe while rendering configured and missing Guide Card data.

## Required Background
{
  "deck_context": {
    "source_summary": "Class 11 of a seven-week AEM Sites course, delivered Monday, August 31, 2026. The audience understands Resources, Sling resolution, editable templates, policies, dialogs, persisted properties and accessible image delivery. This class begins Week 3 by connecting authored Guide Card data to safe, readable HTL and observable DOM states.",
    "core_claim": "HTL should expose a small view contract: prepared values enter, semantic markup and deliberate states are rendered, and each expression is escaped for the context where its output lands.",
    "canonical_facts": [
      "HTL is AEM's preferred server-side template language for HTML.",
      "HTL expressions use ${...}; block statements use data-sly-* attributes.",
      "HTL owns direct markup production while complex business logic belongs in Java such as a Sling Model or service.",
      "data-sly-test conditionally keeps or removes an element.",
      "data-sly-list repeats markup for a collection.",
      "Use an existing semantic HTML element for block statements when possible; use sly only when no suitable element exists.",
      "data-sly-template and data-sly-call reuse small markup fragments with explicit inputs.",
      "HTL automatically applies context-aware escaping for HTML text, attributes and known URI attributes.",
      "URI values such as href and src are validated and unsafe values can be removed.",
      "Expressions inside JavaScript and CSS require explicit display contexts such as scriptString and styleString.",
      "context='unsafe' disables XSS protection and must not be used as a shortcut.",
      "The Guide Card review covers configured, empty-author and empty-visitor outcomes."
    ],
    "canonical_terms": [
      "HTL",
      "data-sly-use",
      "data-sly-test",
      "data-sly-list",
      "data-sly-template",
      "data-sly-call",
      "Sling Model",
      "Resource properties",
      "context-aware escaping",
      "text",
      "attribute",
      "uri",
      "scriptString",
      "styleString",
      "context='unsafe'",
      "configured state",
      "empty state"
    ]
  },
  "slide_local_context": {
    "required_background": "Use a Guide Card fragment with title='Weekend in Mérida', link='/content/wknd/us/en/guides/merida.html' and label='Open guide'. Annotate ${properties.title}, ${card.title} and ${card.link} with source value and final DOM position."
  }
}
